function: Online tracking of BS analog beam angles and RIS reflection angles for mobile users to maximize sum rate, without current position or CSI (p. 7).
system: Downlink mmWave MU-MISO: BS with 4x8 UPA and 2 RF chains, 2 single-antenna users, 2 passive reflecting RISs (8x8); no carrier frequency stated (p. 3, 4, 11).
method: Multi-agent DRL: MADDPG (continuous angles) and dueling MADQN (codebook angles); one agent for BS, one per RIS, common sum-rate reward; online reinforcement learning (p. 7-10).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Saleh-Valenzuela mmWave channel, LoS path-loss exponent 2.7, Gaussian NLoS paths, Markov user mobility; no 3GPP model, dataset, or measurements (p. 4, 5, 11).
test_conditions: Online learning while users move; no separate training and test conditions; speeds, codebooks, RIS size and count, and users varied across simulations (p. 12-15).
baselines: Non-learned: exhaustive codebook search, greedy beam assignment [10], RIS scheme [9] with full BS search, fully digital BCD [47]. Learned: single-agent DDPG and DQN (p. 11-12).
metrics: Average and instantaneous sum rate (bps/Hz), convergence time in time slots, sum-rate degradation under CSI error, angle alignment, per-user rate and Jain's index (p. 12-15).
q1_support: p. 4: "we have adopted this channel model in our work" (Saleh-Valenzuela, a textbook mmWave model); path-loss exponent 2.7 and Gaussian NLoS paths (p. 5, 11); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data.
q2_support: p. 14: "operates in an online learning setting, where policy updates and beam tracking execute simultaneously" - each scenario (speeds, codebooks, RIS count and size, K=4) is learned online in itself; no model trained in one condition and tested in another is reported.
q3_support: p. 12: "consistently achieve faster convergence compared to the single-agent schemes (SADDPG or SADQN)" - the only learned baselines are single-agent variants of the proposed method, compared on convergence (Figs. 6-7); the non-learned Benchmarks 1-4 are compared on sum rate (Figs. 8-11).
q4_support: p. 14: "a simple two-layer structure with 800 neurons in the first hidden layer and 600 neurons in the second hidden layer" and "This design remains computationally lightweight" - qualitative; no operations, parameter count, order or runtime is reported (convergence time in slots, Fig. 7, p. 12, is not a cost).
q5_support: p. 11: "The DRL structure is constructed by using Keras [45] with TensorFlow [46]" - libraries only; no link to code or data, simulated channels, no public dataset or measured data.
notes: Included, area 3: the learned agents set the BS analog beam angles and the RIS reflection angles (p. 7), while the digital zero-forcing beamformer is computed, not learned (p. 6); passive reflecting RISs (p. 4), so ris=1. q1=0 because the Saleh-Valenzuela model is a textbook model in a custom simulator. q2=0 because learning is online inside each scenario, with no train/test split of conditions. q3=0 is a borderline call for the reviewer: SADDPG and SADQN (p. 12) are single-agent forms of the proposed multi-agent method and the text compares them on convergence and stability (Figs. 6-7, p. 12), whereas the earlier-published baselines [9], [10], [47] are non-learned. q4=0 because only layer widths and a qualitative lightweight claim are given (p. 14). q5=0: no release.
